metadata.target_nutrients: Primary nutrients to maximize for each deficiency.
metadata.emphasize: Nutrients to boost absorption or support metabolism.
metadata.tips: Deterministic bioavailability guidance shown to users.

iron.label: Iron Deficiency Anemia
tips: Pair iron-rich meals with Vitamin C (lemon, amla, guava, orange) to triple non-heme iron absorption.
Avoid tea, coffee, and calcium-rich foods within 1 hour of an iron-rich meal - tannins and calcium inhibit iron uptake.
Soak and sprout legumes, and ferment batters (idli/dosa) to break down phytates that bind iron.
Use iron-rich greens (amaranth, drumstick, fenugreek) textured small and cooked lightly to reduce oxalates.
Include small amounts of meat/fish/egg (if diet permits) - heme iron is absorbed 2-3x better than plant iron.
Cook in iron vessels (karahi/skillet) to leach 1-2 mg extra iron into gravies.

anemia.label: Nutritional Anemia (Mixed)
tips: Combination anemia needs all three builders: iron (from greens, legumes, jaggery), folate (green leaves, chickpea), and B12 (dairy, eggs, fish, fortified foods).
Add Vitamin C at every iron meal to improve absorption of non-heme iron.
Avoid tea/coffee/calcium within an hour of iron-heavy meals.
If strictly vegetarian, B12 comes almost only from dairy - consider fortified foods or a supplement on medical advice.
Monitor for 4-6 weeks; dietary correction raises hemoglobin gradually.

b12.label: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
tips: B12 is found almost exclusively in animal foods: milk, paneer, curd, eggs, fish, poultry, and liver.
Strict vegetarians and vegans must rely on dairy (if vegetarian) or fortified foods; consider a cyanocobalamin supplement on medical advice.
The body stores years of B12, so restoration is slow - pair with folate-rich greens for red cell production.
Avoid alcohol excess, which interferes with B12 absorption.

folate.label: Folate (Vitamin B9) Deficiency
tips: Folate is abundant in green leafy vegetables (spinach, amaranth, drumstick), pulses, beetroot, and citrus.
Folate is heat- and light-sensitive - steam or lightly cook greens and eat them fresh.
Pair folate foods with Vitamin C (lemon juice on salads) to protect the vitamin.
Women of childbearing age should meet the 400 ug/day target to prevent neural tube defects.
Avoid excess alcohol and smoking, which deplete folate.

vitamin_d.label: Vitamin D Deficiency
tips: Very few foods naturally contain vitamin D (mushrooms, egg yolk, fatty fish); fortified milk and oils are helpful.
Sun exposure (20-30 minutes, forearms+face, 11am-3pm, 2-4 times/week) is the primary natural source.
Pair vitamin D foods with calcium-rich ones (milk, paneer, sesame, greens) for bone health.
Fat helps vitamin D absorption - cook mushrooms/eggs in a little oil.
Over-supplementation can be toxic; keep total intake near 15 ug/day unless a doctor advises more.

calcium.label: Calcium Deficiency
tips: Dairy (milk, curd, paneer), sesame seeds, amaranth greens, drumstick leaves and ragi are top Indian calcium sources.
Vitamin D is needed to absorb calcium - combine with sun exposure or vitamin-D foods.
Avoid taking calcium with iron-rich meals - they compete for absorption.
Limit excess salt and caffeine which increase calcium loss.

zinc.label: Zinc Deficiency
tips: Meat, eggs, seafood (prawns), and nuts (cashew) provide the most bioavailable zinc.
Vegetarian zinc comes from legumes, nuts and seeds - soak, sprout or ferment to reduce phytate binding.
Pair zinc foods with protein and Vitamin C to improve uptake.
Avoid excess tea/coffee and iron supplements taken simultaneously with zinc meals.

protein.label: Protein Deficiency
tips: Combine cereals+millets with pulses (dal+roti, khichdi) for complete protein.
Add dairy (milk, paneer, curd), eggs, soy, or meat/fish according to your diet preference.
Spread protein across all three meals for better utilization.
Include at least one nut or seed (peanuts, almonds, sesame) daily.
